title: The ordinary coefficient-first projection reduction square
statement: Fix the finite-field datum, $\ell\ne p$, finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and simultaneous reduction models $m$ [def-pur-conventions, def-pur-compactification-reduction-models]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$ between separated finite-type schemes over the datum, with compactification $c$. Choose normalized equivalence data on $X,c.Z,Y$ [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. For integral finite-Tor constructible $K,M$ and an invertible system open inverse factor, use [def-pur-compactification-b-projection-data]. Write $H=f_R^*K\otimes M$, $\pi:K\otimes PM\to PH$ for the ordinary coefficient-first projection, $t_H=\mu\nu:rH\to f_\bullet^*rK\otimes rM$, and $t_V=\mu(1\otimes b_M):r(K\otimes PM)\to rK\otimes F_\bullet rM$. Then $r(\pi)b_HF_\bullet(t_H)=t_V\alpha^\bullet$ as an equality of whole systems (diagrammatic composition). Moreover $\pi$ is natural in both inputs: tensor of $a:K\to K\prime$ and $P(b)$ followed by $\pi_{K\prime,M\prime}$ equals $\pi_{K,M}$ followed by $P(f_R^*a\otimes b)$ for arbitrary ambient integral targets $K\prime,M\prime$. This uses ordinary tensors only; it asserts no completion-unit isomorphisms or completed projection square.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary projection descent, and tower-geometric-gamma.proof.md (2), signed tensor transpose

proof.text: Use ordinary ringed derived operations temporarily, writing $f_R^*$ for ordinary pullback, $H=M\otimes^Lf_R^*K$, $V=PM\otimes^LK$, and $U=PH$. By [det-lem-int-tensor-pullback] and [det-lem-int-tensor-product], $f_R^*K,H$ are derived-complete bounded constructible. By [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower], $PM,PH$ are derived-complete bounded constructible; hence so is $V$ by the tensor theorem. Their reduction systems are normalized by [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. For uniform finite-Tor bounds, pullback preserves a finite interval by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], tensor adds the two intervals by [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], and compact support widens the interval by $2d$ by the direct-image theorem. Thus $r_XM,r_YK,r_XH,r_YV,r_YU$ have the common bounds required below. The finite statements apply to $O/\ell^n=O/\varpi^{en}$, with no unramifiedness assumption.

source.place: Paragraphs (1)-(3), ordinary constructible operations and uniform finite-level bounds

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the middle scheme of $c$. Extension by zero preserves the integral constructible category by [det-lem-int-tensor-shriek], so $j_!M$ is complete, and the ordinary pullbacks and tensors in the proper/open factors are complete by the two ordinary-operation theorems from Step 1, applied also on $Z$. Under Step 2 the projection transformation in [def-exchange-projection] is the ordinary transformation $\pi_R:V\to U$. Indeed the proper factor is characterized by its adjoint transpose: the tensor/pullback comparison followed by $\varepsilon_{p,j_!M}\otimes1$. Identifying a complete ordinary pullback with its completion identifies the adjunction Hom bijection with the ordinary one on these objects; the counit is the adjunct of the same identity. The tensor comparison is the same quotient-balanced comparison of Step 2. Hence the two proper transposes coincide. For the open factor, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] characterizes the inverse tensor map as the adjunct of the open unit tensored with identity; that unit restricts to identity. Both maps therefore have the same open transpose as well. The pullback compositor is the canonical monoidal, adjunction-compatible one of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Composing these identical factors gives the asserted identification of the actual transformations, including their counit and open-unit normalizations.

source.place: Paragraph (3), identifying the ordinary and completed proper/open projection factors

proof.text: For $N=M,H$, the comparison needed for projection descent is the specified $b_N$. To check its normalization, $j$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], since $p_cj=f$ is finite type and $p_c$ is proper, hence quasi-separated. The schemes in $c$ are qcqs. Apply [lem-sp-complete-compactification-limit-realization]: its $\alpha_{c,N}:PN\simeq L_YF_\bullet r_XN$ is $P(u_N)$ followed by the open/limit, proper/limit and scalar-restriction comparisons, all on strict systems. Its reduction transpose is $e_{F_\bullet r_XN}r_Y(\alpha_{c,N})$. The comparison in [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower](2), and hence the $b_N$ fixed in [lem-sp-integral-reconstruction-comparisons], uses exactly this compactification comparison and reconstruction counit. Thus these are the same entire-system map $b_N$, with no change of normalization or choice of evaluated isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (2), the canonical compactification/limit map and its reduction transpose

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-tower-compact-support-projection-formula] with $C_\bullet=r_XM$, $B_\bullet=r_YK$, and the same $c$. Step 1 verifies its uniform constructible finite-Tor hypotheses. It says separately that the proper counit projection and the open unit projection are invertible, and specifies them as actual system maps. Their composite, with the inverse open factor, is the system projection $\theta:F_\bullet r_XM\otimes^Lr_YK\to F_\bullet(r_XM\otimes^Lf_\bullet^*r_YK)$ used below. This verifies both invertibility assumptions of [lem-sp-complete-projection-mate-descent]; its other assumptions are the completeness and bounded-below reductions of $M,K,H,U,V$ from Step 1 and the normalized limit/reconstruction comparisons from Step 4.

source.place: Paragraph (3), the two tower projection factors and the hypotheses of projection descent

proof.text:
Put $a:r_XH\simeq r_XM\otimes^Lf_\bullet^*r_YK$ and $t=(b_M\otimes1)\mu_{PM,K}:r_YV\simeq F_\bullet r_XM\otimes^Lr_YK$. Set $\widetilde\theta=(F_\bullet(a)b_H)^{-1}\theta t:r_YV\to r_YU$. With these exact coordinates [lem-sp-complete-projection-mate-descent] gives $\pi_R=u_U^{-1}L_Y(\widetilde\theta)u_V$. Reducing and using the actual adjunction counit gives
$$r_Y(\pi_R)=e_{r_YU}\,r_YL_Y(\widetilde\theta)\,e_{r_YV}^{-1}=\widetilde\theta.$$
The first equality uses $e_{r_YA}r_Y(u_A)=1$ for $A=U,V$; the second is naturality of $e$. The units and counits are invertible here by [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. Multiplication by $F_\bullet(a)b_H$ gives
$$F_\bullet(a)b_Hr_Y(\pi_R)=\theta(b_M\otimes1)\mu_{PM,K}.$$
This is an equality of whole derived systems, obtained from adjunction identities rather than detected by finite evaluation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), projection descent followed by the actual triangle and naturality identities

proof.text: Use the signed flat K-flat representatives to interchange the tensor factors. Both quotient-balanced paths have the sign (-1)^(ab) on bidegree (a,b), since the quotient scalar has degree zero. TensorReductionModel fixes the comparison on these representatives, and localization gives its symmetry compatibility. Naturality of the actual reconstruction moves P of the inner signed symmetry across b_H. This yields the ordinary coefficient-first projection square.

Compose the ordinary proper/open projection naturality squares from descent with the two signed tensor symmetry naturality squares. No constructibility of the target objects is required for naturality.

lean.statement: theorem ordinary_projection_reduction_square (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (X Y : Over (Scheme.Spec.obj (op (CommRingCat.of D.k)))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] [IsSeparated Y.hom] (f : X ⟶ Y) (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f.left] [IsSeparated f.left] (c : Compactification f.left) (AX : SpNormalizedEquivalence l E X.left (m.abelian X.left) (m.red X.left)) (AZ : SpNormalizedEquivalence l E c.Z (m.abelian c.Z) (m.red c.Z)) (AY : SpNormalizedEquivalence l E Y.left (m.abelian Y.left) (m.red Y.left)) (K : finiteTorConstructibleIntegralCategory l E Y.left) (M : finiteTorConstructibleIntegralCategory l E X.left) (hOpen : IsIso (systemOpenInverse l E m c.i ((red l E m X.left).obj M.obj) ((VaryingRing.G (rings l E) (transitions l E) c.g).obj ((red l E m Y.left).obj K.obj)))) : ((red l E m Y.left).map (ordinaryAlpha l E m c K.obj M.obj) ≫ reconstruction l E m c AX AZ AY (ordinaryInner l E m f.left K.obj M.obj) ≫ (systemImage l E c).map ((m.tensor X.left).hom.app ((ringedPull l E f.left).obj K.obj, M.obj) ≫ (m.systems X.left).closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom ((m.pull f.left).hom.app K.obj) (𝟙 _))) = (m.tensor Y.left).hom.app (K.obj, (integralImage l E c).obj M.obj) ≫ (m.systems Y.left).closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 _) (reconstruction l E m c AX AZ AY M.obj)) ≫ systemAlpha l E m c ((red l E m Y.left).obj K.obj) ((red l E m X.left).obj M.obj) hOpen) ∧ (∀ (K' : CompleteProjectionDescent.Integral l E Y.left) (M' : CompleteProjectionDescent.Integral l E X.left) (a : K.obj ⟶ K') (b : M.obj ⟶ M'), (m.integral.tensor Y.left).ordinary.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom a ((integralImage l E c).map b)) ≫ ordinaryAlpha l E m c K' M' = ordinaryAlpha l E m c K.obj M.obj ≫ (integralImage l E c).map ((m.integral.tensor X.left).ordinary.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom ((ringedPull l E f.left).map a) b)))
